span.p:
Course Value
Almost no real business question is answerable from a single
table — JOIN is the single most-used clause in professional SQL

div.style: color: rgb(26, 32, 44) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 620px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Real-Life Value
'Revenue by loyalty tier' or 'customers who never ordered' need
two tables talking to each other — this is exactly how

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;
color: rgb(26, 32, 44) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 620px; text-align: center;

span.p:
By the end, you can…
Explain why real data lives in separate related tables, write an
INNER JOIN to combine matching rows, write a LEFT JOIN to keep
unmatched rows too, and combine a JOIN with WHERE/GROUP BY
